The must-sees

9 places Wizzy will tap you for first, each with a story and something to look for.

  1. 01
    Church · 1731

    Basilica of Superga

    Victor Amadeus II vowed to build it if Turin survived the siege of 1706, and Filippo Juvarra designed it. In 1949 a plane carrying the Grande Torino football team crashed into the hillside behind it; a memorial stands there.

    Look for

    From the terrace on a clear day, look south-west for Monviso, the lone pyramid peak on the Alpine skyline.

  2. 02
    Museum · 1824

    Egyptian Museum

    Founded in 1824, it is the oldest museum in the world devoted entirely to ancient Egypt. Its statue galleries include a seated figure of Ramesses II.

    Look for

    Find the tomb of Kha and Merit, found untouched in 1906, still holding bread, clothes and furniture packed for their afterlife.

  3. 03
    Landmark · 1889

    Mole Antonelliana

    Alessandro Antonelli began it in 1863 as a synagogue, but the Jewish community gave it up as costs rose and the city finished it in 1889. It now houses the National Cinema Museum.

  4. 04
    Palace

    Palazzo Madama

    It grew from a Roman gate into a medieval castle, and Filippo Juvarra added the grand façade and staircase in the early 18th century. It houses the city’s Museum of Ancient Art and was the seat of the first Senate of the Kingdom of Italy.

    Look for

    Walk round to the back: the two brick towers there are from the Roman gate the castle grew out of.

  5. 05
    Square

    Piazza Castello

    For centuries this was the seat of Savoy power, laid out around the old castle. Arcaded streets lead from here towards the river and the station.

    Look for

    In one corner, the plain front of San Lorenzo hides Guarino Guarini’s dome, a lattice of crossing arches.

  6. 06
    Square

    Piazza San Carlo

    The statue of Duke Emanuele Filiberto sheathing his sword, by Carlo Marochetti, is known locally as the Caval ’d Brons. The arcades hold some of the city’s historic cafés.

    Look for

    Under the arcade by Caffè Torino, a brass bull is set into the pavement. People step on it for luck.

  7. 07
    Palace

    Reggia di Venaria

    Charles Emmanuel II of Savoy built it as a hunting residence in the second half of the 17th century. After a long decline it was restored and reopened in 2007.

    Look for

    Walk the Great Gallery by Filippo Juvarra, a long white hall lit by tall windows on both sides.

  8. 08
    Palace

    Royal Palace of Turin

    It was the main residence of the House of Savoy from the 17th century. The Royal Library in the complex keeps a red-chalk drawing believed to be Leonardo’s self-portrait.

    Look for

    On the gate pillars stand Castor and Pollux, the twin horsemen of myth, placed there as guardians.

  9. 09
    Church

    Turin Cathedral

    Built in the 1490s, it is the only Renaissance church in the city. The Shroud is kept in a chapel here and shown in public only on rare occasions.

    Look for

    Behind the cathedral, Guarini’s Chapel of the Holy Shroud rises as a dark, stepped cone of stacked arches.
